note.text: A report presents information for a stated reader and purpose. A heading, introduction, organised findings and a conclusion or recommendations can help. Exact format depends on the task. Separate what was observed from an inference and from what should happen next. Use clear factual wording and appropriate tense. A fictional classroom report must be labelled as such; it should not claim that a real school event or inspection occurred. A report differs from a story seeking suspense or an essay primarily defending a personal preference.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to organise findings and recommendations while separating observation, inference and proposal. Builds on: narrative chronology, audience and formal-purpose writing. Leads to: later evidence-based summaries and reports.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: FICTIONAL CLASSROOM REPORT: Reading-room materials. Purpose: to review the model room’s organisation. Findings: some books were placed away from their labelled shelves, and the borrowing notice was not easily visible. The record does not establish who moved the books. Recommendation: place the notice where readers can see it and agree how returned materials are sorted. A later check should establish whether the arrangement works. Prepared by an imaginary club secretary.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the reader, purpose and permitted information. Group findings logically and link each recommendation to a finding. Do not invent a responsible person when the evidence does not identify one. Check headings, sentence accuracy and whether an inference is being presented as if directly observed.

Findings: some books were placed away from their labelled shelves, and the borrowing notice was not easily visible. The record does not establish who moved the books. Recommendation: place the notice where readers can see it and agree how returned materials are sorted. A later check should establish whether the arrangement works. Prepared by an imaginary club secretary.
checklist: My headings and order suit the purpose.
I distinguish findings, inferences and recommendations.
